title: Transactional LLM: Consumption & Packaging Playbook
author: Claire Nguyen
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines Redwood’s recommended packaging, consumption primitives, and go-to-market considerations for Transactional LLM features — defined as low-latency, request-driven text generation used inside user-facing product flows (chat widgets, transactional composition, code suggestions, and short-answer APIs). The intent is to provide a single source of truth for product, pricing, and engineering teams to design plans that balance predictable unit economics, latency SLOs, and straightforward customer onboarding.

Scope and definitions
---------------------
- Transactional LLM workload: per-request generation with 16–1024 token outputs, median request size typically < 256 input tokens, bursty spikes tied to user events.
- Consumption primitives: per-token generation billing, bundling (monthly credits), and SLA-backed reserved throughput (Dedicated).
- Target customers: SaaS products embedding realtime suggestions, marketplaces calling generation at user interaction time, and internal enterprise UI features (CRMs, code review tools).

Design goals
------------
1. Predictable per-unit economics for customers adopting within product flows.
2. Straightforward mapping from latency SLO to price and packaging.
3. Migration path from hosted (self-serve) to Dedicated/Private with minimal friction.
4. Low cognitive overhead for developers integrating the API (clear defaults, tiered bundling).

Key product primitives and packaging options
--------------------------------------------
- Pay-as-you-go (HOSTED): per-token pricing for generation and embeddings; default for small/experimental customers. No SLA beyond standard hosted uptime. Ideal for dev/test and small PLG growth.
- Commitment bundles (CREDIT PACKS): 30/90/365-day credit packages sold as monthly-equivalent commitments. Credits consume at per-token-equivalent rates and can have rollover rules depending on enterprise tier.
- Dedicated capacity add-on (DEDICATED): reserved throughput measured in tokens-per-second or requests-per-minute with latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99). Includes backfill credits for short-term overage during bursts for a limited budget.
- Hybrid fidelity tokens (FLEX-FID): split credits for low/medium/high fidelity outputs, enabling customers to use cheaper low-fidelity paths for bulk background tasks while preserving high fidelity for primary user flows.

Pricing matrix (guidance)
-------------------------
Use this table as the canonical mapping for packaging discussions. Values are guidance and may be adjusted per customer or region.

| Package | Typical customer size | Billing metric | Default latency SLO | Notes |
|--------:|----------------------:|:---------------|:-------------------:|:-----|
| HOSTED PAYG | Individual dev / early PLG | Per 1K tokens generated | None (best-effort) | Quick onboard, free credits for 14 days |
| STANDARD CREDIT PACK (monthly equiv) | SMBs | Credits (tokens) | p95 < 400 ms for 256 tokens | 5% rollover; usage analytics included |
| ENTERPRISE CREDIT PACK + SUPPORT | Mid-market | Credits + committed peak throughput | p95 < 250 ms for 256 tokens; p99 < 800 ms | Dedicated support; reserved capacity options |
| DEDICATED SLO (enterprise) | Large customers | Monthly reserved throughput + overage credits | p95 < 120 ms for 128 tokens; p99 < 400 ms | SLA & uptime crediting; regional affinity |

Billing and metering rules
--------------------------
- Tokens are metered as input + output tokens per request.
- Credits convert to tokens at a model-specific conversion multiplier (documented per model in the catalog). Multipliers account for quantized models, sequence length, and fan-out.
- Rollover: standard credit packs allow up to 5% rollover for 30-day packs, 20% for annual packs, configurable for enterprise contracts.
- Overage: for committed bundles, automatic short-term bursting is allowed up to a defined percentage (default 20%) and debited using pay-as-you-go rates unless an overage credit pool exists.

SLO-to-price mapping and decision flow
-------------------------------------
When evaluating a customer request for SLO-backed packaging, follow this decision flow:
1. Capture observed per-request token distribution and 95th percentile latency requirement.
2. Determine candidate service tier: HOSTED (no SLO), STANDARD CREDIT, or DEDICATED SLO.
3. Simulate cost using the customer’s expected qps and token distribution. Use the Redwood Optimize simulator to estimate token-convert multipliers.
4. Recommend packaging: if p95 target <= 250 ms and qps consistent > 2k rps sustained, recommend Dedicated; else recommend Standard Credit with optional burst cushions.

Operational requirements (engineering checklist)
------------------------------------------------
- Telemetry: per-tenant per-route breakdown of tokens, latency buckets (p50/p95/p99), error class counts, and model-variant usage.
- Observability dashboards: Billing delta, committed vs actual throughput, burst events, and model fallback rate.
- Alerts: Trigger on breach of 3 consecutive p95 SLO violations within a 10-minute window, unexplained model fallback > 2% of requests in 5m.
- Deployment: Support for region affinity, prewarm pools in Dedicated, and highway routing for low-latency traffic.

Table: SLO monitoring thresholds
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Owner |
|:------|:------------------|:-------------------|:------|
| p95 latency (256 token baseline) | > 250 ms for 5 min | > 350 ms for 2 min | infra-performance |
| model-fallback-rate | > 0.5% sustained 10m | > 2% sustained 5m | runtime-team |
| burst overage spend | > 30% of monthly budget | > 60% of monthly budget | commercial-ops |

Transition playbook: Self-serve -> Dedicated
-------------------------------------------
1. Eligibility check: usage history crossing committed thresholds (configurable: sustained 14 days with avg qps > threshold) or customer-requested SLA.
2. Cost simulation and proposed committed throughput (finance + product).
3. Provisioning: create Dedicated pool, configure tenant routing policies and affinity, and prewarm KV caches.
4. Canary migration: shift 5% traffic for 2 hours, evaluate latency/error/fallback, then 25%, then 100% over 48–72 hours.
5. Post-migration: add to SLO monitoring, finalize billing terms, and schedule QBR.

Roadmap alignment and near-term initiatives (next 6 months)
----------------------------------------------------------
- H1: Launch FLEX-FID credit types and runtime tagging for fidelity buckets to enable mixed-fidelity consumption on the same tenant.
- H2: Built-in cost simulator inside Console that maps a customer’s observed traffic to recommended packages and estimated monthly spend.
- H3: Beta of regional Dedicated pools and automated affinity routing to reduce p95 by ~15% for cross-region customers.
- Ongoing: Tighten default p95 targets by optimizing kernel selection and KV prefetch heuristics in runtime.

Go-to-market and enablement checklist
-----------------------------------
- Sales collateral: one-pager illustrating SLO tiers, migration path, and common customer archetypes.
- Playbooks for Solutions Engineers: scripted Q&A to determine packaging fit and to run the cost simulator during discovery.
- Launch plan: staged availability (hosted -> SMB credit -> enterprise credit -> dedicated), with targeted beta customers for each stage.

Release notes (initial public launch)
-----------------------------------
- Version: transactional-packaging-v1 (released 2027-01-12)
- Highlights: Introduced FLEX-FID token types, standardized credit rollover rules, and SLO-backed Dedicated offering.
- Breaking changes: credit conversion multipliers now model-specific (customers on older plans will be notified with a 60-day migration window).
- Known limitations: Console cost simulator is beta and does not yet account for per-request function/tool-calls; Dedicated regional pools available only in us-west and eu-central for initial launch.

Appendix A: Example customer scenario
-----------------------------------
Customer: SaaS analytics SaaSCo wants in-app insights via a realtime assistant.
- Observed traffic: median 50 rps, 95th 300 rps bursts; median request 120 input+output tokens.
- Recommended packaging: STANDARD CREDIT monthly with 10% burst cushion; migrate to DEDICATED if sustained qps > 2k for 14 continuous days.
- Estimated monthly spend (guidance): $X per 1M tokens using model-a-multiplier 1.0.

Appendix B: Open questions & decisions
-------------------------------------
- Decision needed: Default rollover percentage for 90-day vs 365-day packs (finance owns).
- Question: Should fidelity buckets be exposed as separate SKUs or internal tagging only? (Product/Commercial to decide).
